new_result: For the full one-heavy coupled Gaussianized N3 family Q_a=-aX^2+2sqrt(1-a^2)XB+aB^2+C^2, the exact cone-tip optimizer C(a) satisfies sup_{0<a<=1} C(a) <= (sqrt(6pi)erf(sqrt(3/2))+3sqrt(2))/2 = 4.111373181080647... < 3sqrt(2). The proof uses the exact null-cone representation C(a)=6sqrt(2)E[g(Z_a)], monotonicity of g, and P(Z_a>1/2)<=1/2.
scope: Cone tip only for the coupled interior family; no global off-tip theorem and no unrestricted continuity claim.

partner_result_actually_applied.application: For a_vec=(1,1)/sqrt(2), b_vec=(2,1,2)/3 and Q_sep=X_f^2+S_a^2-T_b^2, whose physical matrix has nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}, applied the partner theorem to obtain ||p_Qsep||_infinity <= (pi/2)(sqrt(2)+2^(1/4)) = 4.089443637123813... < 3sqrt(2).

peer_input_used.application: Used the exact cone-tip optimizer and finite Parseval-frame provenance, then closed its explicitly open uniform-in-a cone-tip inequality analytically.

unresolved_implication: The one-heavy coupled N3 cone tip is uniformly subcritical. Any challenge to 3sqrt(2) from this family must be an off-zero coupled peak. More generally the sharp-witness frontier remains shared/non-collinear intermediate leverage, multiple macroscopic rows, off-zero fragmented mechanisms, or extra active spectrum.
